verdict.headline: You carry unlimited liability while the vendor's is capped at one month of fees.
summary: Liability is one-sided: yours is unlimited, the vendor's is tiny.
The contract renews itself unless you give 90 days' notice.
Disputes fall under Delaware law, far from home.

findings.title: Foreign governing law
findings.quote: this agreement is governed by the laws of the state of delaware.
findings.why_risky: Any dispute would be argued under United States law, which is costly for a Malaysian business.
findings.standard: The law of the customer's country, or a neutral nearby one such as Singapore.
findings.suggested_ask: Please change the governing law to the laws of Malaysia.

findings.title: Unlimited liability for you only
findings.quote: The Customer shall be liable without limit for any loss suffered by the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: One mistake could cost you any amount, with no ceiling.
findings.standard: Both sides' liability is capped at the fees paid over 12 months.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the liability cap mutual, at 12 months of fees.

citations.excerpt: MODEL-WRITTEN TEXT THAT MUST BE REPLACED

findings.title: Vendor's liability capped at one month of fees
findings.quote: The Vendors total liability is limited to the fees paid in the one month before a claim
findings.why_risky: If the vendor loses your data, you could recover only one month of fees.
findings.standard: A cap of 12 months of fees, with exceptions for data breaches.
findings.suggested_ask: Please raise the vendor's cap to 12 months of fees.
findings.policy_breach: Your policy requires vendor liability of at least 12 months of fees.

findings.title: Auto-renewal with a 90-day notice window
findings.quote: renews automatically for successive 12 month terms unless the Customer gives 90 days written notice
findings.why_risky: Miss the 90-day window and you are locked in for another year.
findings.standard: Renewal with 30 days' notice, or a reminder from the vendor.
findings.suggested_ask: Please shorten the notice period to 30 days.

findings.title: Broad indemnity
findings.quote: The Customer shall indemnify the Vendor against all claims whatsoever arising in any way.
findings.why_risky: This quote does not exist in the contract; the verifier must drop it.
findings.standard: Each side indemnifies for its own breach.

missing_clauses.title: No data protection clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The vendor handles your financial records but promises nothing about keeping them safe.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a clause committing to PDPA-compliant handling and breach notification.

key_dates.label: Last day to cancel before the agreement renews for another 12 months
key_dates.rule: 90 days before the end of the first 12-month term

key_dates.label: Agreement starts
key_dates.rule: The contract names no effective date
